title: Optional SRStack external research evidence interchange, version 1
description: An optional, extensible interchange for host-authorized external evidence, not an authoritative dataset, storage policy, required workflow, or completeness certificate. Never include credentials, secret URLs, provider API keys, or wallet secrets. Schema validity establishes shape only; it does not authenticate sources, validate arithmetic, reconcile references, or prove coverage. Unknown and partial observations remain useful. Retain conflicting observations and reorg alternatives rather than overwriting them.

headers.description: Reusable header observations keyed by decimal chain_id + ':' + block_hash. Values must agree with their keys; cross-field consistency requires a consumer check. Keep competing block hashes at the same height. Canonicality is an observation at a stated check time, not a permanent property. Reuse a fetched header per distinct hash; recheck canonicality and refetch when reorgs or conflicting evidence warrant it.

unresolved_headers.description: Optional partial header observations that do not yet have a usable chain/hash cache key.

events.description: Raw observations, including removed records and conflicting duplicates. Not an already reconciled purchase ledger.

assumptions.description: User choices, mathematical scenarios, attribution conventions and unproved semantics; keep separate from observations.

results.description: Derived outputs with their input references, formulas, units and qualifications; not new source observations. Preserve exact integers/rationals as strings.

decimal.description: Nonnegative integer encoded without binary-floating-point conversion.

timestamp.description: Source observation/retrieval/check time. This is not the chain header timestamp. Format checking depends on the chosen validator.

sourceRefs.description: References to source ids. Unknown provenance can use an empty list; consumers check that supplied references resolve.

identity.description: Original public source identity, such as a document URL, index/export identity or RPC method and public provider label. Remove credentials and secret query parameters; do not store an access token as provenance.

query.description: Optional public filters, block anchors, pagination and method parameters, never secrets.

timestamp.description: Header Unix timestamp in integer seconds, or unknown. Never substitute retrieval time or an estimated block time.

alternatives.description: Conflicting or earlier observations for this same chain/hash. Reorg replacement hashes occupy their own cache entries.

asset.description: Authenticated asset identity, not a ticker assumed to mean USD. A fictional fixture must label it fictional.

status.description: Whether this observation matched a checked receipt log, not whether discovery is complete or a refund is proved.

generation.description: Authenticated generation identity or unknown; same round number across emitters is not the same round.

log_index.description: Ethereum block-global log index, not a transaction-local event counter.

removed.description: The source's removed flag, not independent proof of present canonicality.

header_ref.description: Optional explicit chain_id:block_hash key into headers; consumers check consistency with event identity.

decoded.description: Decoded observations only; missing fields or unknown values do not mean zero. Event ABI meaning and price/quantity semantics need separate authentication.

pagination.description: Optional cursor/page/exhaustion observations; an exhausted list proves only its supported scope.

range.description: Inclusive block interval in the stated chain/emitter/generation/filter scope. Unknown bounds stay unknown. Consumers check ordering and overlap; JSON Schema cannot establish range union or semantic completeness.

counts.description: Descriptive work/record counts only, never a completeness proof.

coverage.description: Discovery, log/index scan scope, receipt matching, header canonicality and historical-close claims are distinct. Empty arrays mean no supplied range evidence, not complete coverage or zero events. Overlaps/conflicts and gaps may be retained; a caller must reconcile them for its specific claim. No closed-world census is required to exchange useful partial evidence.
